content: 1. Fosphenytoin reduces the plasma levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely when co-administering these drugs. 2. Griseofulvin decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Careful monitoring is recommended during concurrent use. 3. Iloperidone increases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. As a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor, iloperidone may elevate plasma concentrations of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. Monitor closely. 4. Levonorgestrel oral contraceptives may reduce the efficacy of insulin degludec due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Progestins, including levonorgestrel, can impair glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 5. Levonorgestrel oral contraceptives may decrease the effects of insulin aspart and inhaled insulin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. Monitor blood glucose levels in patients with diabetes. 6. Istradefylline increases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. At a dose of 40 mg/day, istradefylline has been shown to increase the peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates. Consider dose adjustments for sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 7. Ivosidenib decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Co-administration may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Consider alternative contraceptive methods and monitor closely. 8. Levonorgestrel oral contraceptives reduce the levels of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance, likely due to induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of lamotrigine. 9. Lenacapavir increases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This effect may persist for up to 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir. Monitor for potential adverse reactions and adjust doses of CYP3A4 substrates as needed. 10. Levonorgestrel oral contraceptives may reduce the effects of liraglutide due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives can impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 11. Levonorgestrel oral contraceptives increase the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may increase the risk of toxicity. Monitor closely. 12. Levonorgestrel oral contraceptives reduce the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor glycemic control in patients receiving this combination. 13. Mifepristone reduces the efficacy of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use a backup contraceptive method during co-administration. 14. Mitotane decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4. Monitor for reduced efficacy of CYP3A4 substrates and adjust dosages as necessary. 15. Mycophenolate reduces the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives through an unspecified mechanism. Consider additional birth control methods during mycophenolate therapy. 16. Nafcillin decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for reduced contraceptive efficacy. 17. Nemolizumab decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by increasing CYP enzyme activity through cytokine suppression. Monitor for reduced systemic levels of narrow therapeutic index CYP substrates and adjust dosages as needed. 18. Nevirapine decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for reduced contraceptive efficacy. 19. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for reduced contraceptive effectiveness. 20. Pentobarbital decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for reduced efficacy. 21. Phenobarbital decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for reduced contraceptive effectiveness. 22. Phenytoin decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for reduced efficacy. 23. Pitolisant decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. As a weak CYP3A4 inducer, pitolisant may reduce the effectiveness of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Monitor closely. 24. Primidone decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for reduced contraceptive efficacy. 25. Ribociclib increases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for potential adverse effects. 26. Rifabutin decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for reduced contraceptive effectiveness. 27. Rifampin decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for reduced efficacy. 28. Rifapentine decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for reduced contraceptive effectiveness. 29. Rucaparib increases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust dosages of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 30. Siltuximab may restore CYP450 enzymatic activity by inhibiting IL-6, which is downregulated during infection and inflammation. Use caution when co-administering with CYP substrates that have a narrow therapeutic index. 31. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for reduced contraceptive efficacy. 32. Stiripentol affects CYP3A4 metabolism as both an inducer and inhibitor. Monitor for increased or decreased effects of CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol, and adjust dosages as needed. 33. Tazemetostat decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for reduced contraceptive effectiveness. 34. Tecovirimat decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. As a weak CYP3A4 inducer, monitor for reduced effectiveness of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 35. Teriflunomide increases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives through an unknown mechanism. Monitor closely for potential adverse effects. 36. Tesamorelin decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by altering metabolism. Use alternative contraception methods during co-administration. 37. Topiramate decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for reduced contraceptive efficacy. 38. Valoctocogene roxaparvovec may increase the risk of hepatotoxicity when combined with medications that elevate liver enzymes. Monitor closely and consider alternative medications if potential drug interactions are identified. 39. Acetazolamide increases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 40. Anastrozole increases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 41. Cyclophosphamide increases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 42. Danazol increases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 43. Drospirenone increases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 44. Enasidenib may increase or decrease the concentrations of combined hormonal contraceptives through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 45. Larotrectinib increases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 46. Levoketoconazole increases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 47. Albiglutide’s hypoglycemic effects may be reduced by levonorgestrel oral contraceptives due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 48. Amobarbital decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for reduced contraceptive efficacy. 49. Antithrombin alfa and levonorgestrel oral contraceptives may antagonize each other pharmacodynamically, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 50. Apalutamide decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute another drug when possible. Evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect if co-administration is necessary. 51. Argatroban and levonorgestrel oral contraceptives may antagonize each other pharmacodynamically, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 52. Atazanavir may increase or decrease the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use alternatives if available. 53. Belzutifan decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive failure or breakthrough bleeding may occur. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective non-hormonal contraception. 54. Bemiparin and levonorgestrel oral contraceptives may antagonize each other pharmacodynamically, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 55. Bivalirudin and levonorgestrel oral contraceptives may antagonize each other pharmacodynamically, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 56. Bosentan decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for reduced contraceptive efficacy. 57. Brigatinib decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive failure may occur. Women should use effective non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. 58. Calaspargase pegol may indirectly interact with oral contraceptives, reducing their efficacy. Use alternative non-oral contraceptive methods for females of childbearing potential. 59. Carbamazepine decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for reduced contraceptive efficacy. 60. Cenobamate decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Advise women to use additional or alternative non-hormonal birth control methods. 61. Ceritinib increases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for potential adverse effects. 62. Clobazam decreases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Additional non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 63. Crofelemer increases the levels of levonorgestrel oral contraceptives by inhibiting CYP3A4 in the gut. Systemic inhibition is unlikely due to minimal absorption. 64. Cyclosporine and levonorgestrel oral contraceptives may increase each other’s levels by reducing metabolism. Monitor closely for potential adverse effects.
